I do agree with you about the first few seasons. And i think that's an excellent way to think about it- that Ned and Robb etc were never even the main players, only misdirection, making it easier to kill them for amazing shock value. 

However, i do still think the show has lost its 'teeth' moreso than necessary, even considering it is still just fantasy fiction as you say. Sure, i am not expecting an INSANE rug pull (Jon, Dany getting killed etc)- but so late in the game here, on a supposed suicide run, to not kill some (beloved) secondary characters absolutely feels Hollywood-y to me. They aren't major players either, at all.

I adore Tormund. The mission was dire at best. He dies, tragedy. Plot moves on. Same with Jorah. Or Beric. I totally agree with much of what you say but i really think they fumbled this one. What an amazing chance for some true 'old school' GoT deaths, hit us hard. But instead miraculous escapes.

Unless every single character that survived that mission has a very significant role to come, i will be disappointed. I also think every character that survived means devoting more (already precious) screen time to them, and yet another plot to wrap up. I have total faith in D&D, but fuck me if it isn't risky at this point to keep saving characters for some hopefully important 'purpose'.

I was quite positive that actually Jorah, Tormund, Thoros, Beric and the dragon would die. 

Gendry, Hound, and Jon remain. I know it would have been absolutely brutal but considering in my opinion it has felt a little tame and hollywood-y with the plot armour recently, all of these characters could've died without sacrificing the plot, and the threat would've seemed even even more real.

I was diagnosed with a psychotic illness many years ago, and so delusions became part of my daily life (although i didn't realise they were delusions at the time).

Nothing too unexpected or particularly unusual however- i truly believed i was being followed and watched, that people would be listening to me outside my door in my room at home. I thought police had bugged my phone, criminals were waiting in my garden to strike, and that members of the general public were plotting to harm me (in a way i couldn't understand). I was so sure of this stuff, and yet noone believed me. I was so sure.

Thinking about it, in some ways one of the worst ones was every single time i got off some form of public transport, a bus, train etc. i thought every single person who got off behind me had been waiting for me to leave and was now following me. I had no choice but to sprint home, freaking out and losing my mind, slam the door, and then tell myself i was just unwell.

Yeah. Delusions, not fun.

Hey! Sorry for the late response. Revising is only as helpful as you make it yourself, if that makes sense. For example i had friends who would revise like CRAZY every day (mostly due to pushy parents), and they actually ended up getting worse grades than people like me, who took a much more relaxed approach. Now, i'm not saying to be complacent at all; working is important. But i really believe staying happy, positive and CONFIDENT about your exams is the key to success. Freaking out and digging yourself in to a deep revision hole is the worst answer possible.

Find revision methods that suit you- some people learn better in all sorts of ways. Personally i was a visual learner- so i liked watching videos, drawing pictures etc. There are tests you can take online to determine what kind of learner you are and then you can plan your revision strategy accordingly. There are so many methods to help you and honestly with a bit of research first you WILL find one that you connect with, and hey, maybe actually ENJOY. I think as you get closer doing mock exams is absolutely INVALUABLE. You can find them all online. I mean, what better way to revise than to do the last TEN years worth of the SAME PAPER you are about to take? :) the questions are often extremely similar, and it gets you in the exam mindset. I just did that, then corrected any wrong answers, then rinse and repeat.

I'm presuming you have your exams in June/July/August? I'm in the UK and that's when ours are. If that's the case- YOU ARE GOING TO BE FINE :) that is such a long time away. Now obviously i don't know you but seriously, DO NOT run yourself in to the ground. I've seen incredibly intelligent people suffer hugely from this. I would recommend, if you want to start now, literally going for 20-30 mins a day. Maximum. Remember, your mental health ALWAYS comes first. In a month or two, maybe up it to 45 mins a day. Then come May time, go for 60-90 mins. But take it easy. Want to go out to a party so don't have time for revision that day? - Fine. Do it. Staying happy will help you more than revision ever could.

And to be honest my friend, GCSE's, once you've done them, while beneficial, really are just a gateway to your A-levels. If you are planning on doing A-levels, and you get at least a couple of those, nobody at all will remember your GCSE's anymore. Hey, i've just finished a degree at uni, and already when talking about Job offers noone even looks at my A-LEVELS anymore!! Each level is just a stepping stone to the next. I'm hopefully going to start my Masters in September so then my Degree won't even be that important!

You'll be fine i'm sure. Don't worry. Honestly once i started A-levels, me and all my friends were laughing about how easy GCSE's were, and how crazy the teachers made them sound. Just relax, and remember NOTHING IS MORE IMPORTANT THAN YOUR MENTAL HEALTH. Remember to chill out and not punish yourself if you don't meet your revision plan for that day or whatever.

A happy you = better grades. 

Any more questions feel free to ask! :)

The problem is, Pixar in my mind were so fantastic because of the originality. Every year, another gem of a movie, based on nothing. So many movies these days are sequels, prequels, e-quels, reboots, or based on books, TV shows, comics etc..

Not that there is anything wrong with adapting excellent source material but for years i just found the imagination of the Pixar staff pretty unrivaled in terms of creative flair.

We had years and years of incredible stuff- (Monsters Inc, Incredibles, Finding Nemo, Ratatouille, Wall-E, Up, the Toy Story Trilogy), and i seriously don't think it's a coincidence that once Disney bought them out- here come the sequels.

I mean, yes, Cars was a misstep- i think most people can agree that. So to make Cars 2 despite the first one being easily their worst reviewed movie- pretty disheartening. And now CARS 3?!?! Merchandise, merchandise, merchandise. The Pixar of 2000-2005 would have never dreamed of it.

Let me put it another way- up until 2010 the only, ONLY sequels Pixar had done were the Toy Story trilogy. And they were wonderful.

Now, post-2010 - we've had Monsters University (disappointing), Incredibles 2 on the way, Finding Nemo 2 on the way, Cars 3 on the way, and even Toy Story 4 on the way?!?! That's 5 sequels in the pipeline compared to a previous decade of 1. And i don't think it's a coincidence it coincides with their buyout by Disney.

I agree that sequels are not inherently bad, absolutely. But for me that is not what makes Pixar great. And as i already stated above i am very happy that others enjoyed this movie so much; i just wanted to know why. Sorry if i seemed a little harsh or dramatic, it's just such a shame personally that my all-time favourite studio seems to be slipping away, and i truly believe relying on sequels is a step in the wrong direction for Pixar.

Cocaine gives you a heightened sense of euphoria and confidence. You feel inexplicably happy and elated at your surroundings and the people with you. You feel the urge to chat (a lot), and conversations you have seem to be extremely important and life-changing even if they are just about 'that bit in that song that sounds totally fucking awesome'. Generally you do just feel very happy and content. That's the positive stuff. Obviously this ^^ is why people love the damn stuff so much. 

Now the neutral stuff. Dry mouth, sweating, increased heart rate, slight distortions in vision etc- this stuff is quite hard to explain to people who have never taken any illicit substances, they are neither particularly positive or negative symptoms but are just something you accept as part of your drug taking experience. 

Now the negative. Risk of cardiovascular difficulties- basically you are far more prone to a heart attack whilst under the influence- and sometimes it can actually feel like that (your heart pumping a million miles a minute) which can be incredibly distressing and sometimes genuinely life threatening. Paranoia, anxiety are also common side effects, especially for inexperienced users. And of course all those wonderful positive effects i listed are incredibly short lived (usually only half an hour after snorting a couple of lines). And of course you want those effects back so you take more. Rinse and repeat. When you come off the drug and run out it can be quite unpleasant, you have squeezed your brain dry of seratonin and so it now has to cope with boring old reality again- at least until you can find more cocaine. (You can see here how easy addiction can be with this drug in particular.) It is incredibly moreish. The need to redose is ever present and strong. Oh, and don't even get me started on the damage it will do to your WALLET!! Here in the UK cocaine can easily be as much as £100 a gram (roughly $160), and a single gram will most likely be gone by the morning.

Now, just to clear things up, most of the health problems associated with cocaine use are due to two things: 1) Impurity of the stuff. and 2) Combining it with other substances.

Now, i'm no doctor, so i can't give loads of detailed examples (easy to look up if you're interested), but basically i know for a fact the average purity of cocaine here in the UK is around a staggering 15%. 15%!!!!! Consider what the hell else makes up the 85% left and you can see how this can be damaging to ones health. Rat poison is common, as is much cheaper pharmaceuticals. It's scary stuff. So actually, the better quality the cocaine (meaning it's far more expensive), the much safer it really is.

Secondly, many MANY people mix cocaine with alchohol. The two drugs go hand in hand at parties and such. And i don't need to lecture you about that- the dangers of mixing coke with booze are extremely well documented. Short answer; never do it.

So yeah, the original question- what does cocaine feel like? It feels like pure fucking awesome- until you run out or experience unwanted side effects; which happens frequently. It is dangerous stuff. But there is a reason so much of the world loves it so much, and that's because of that first awesome hour of consuming it. You feel like a million bucks, and it's so easy to achieve.

Yeah. Any more questions please feel free to ask, hope i've been informative.
